by Starkeeper (MrLiwai)

Summary

Phainon has survived 33,550,336 time loops. He remembers everything. No one else does—except for Mydeimos, the crown prince who, in one rare loop, finally saw him.
But just when Phainon dares to hope, Mydeimos vanishes.
Trapped in a cycle where pain is constant and love doesn’t exist, Phainon makes a final, desperate choice to end it all—
Only to wake up somewhere new.
A different world. Familiar people and a language he doesn’t understand.

And one question echoing in his mind:
If Mydeimos is here too… will he remember him?

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The new start
chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

33,550,336 circles.
137 people.
13 distinct areas.

Passages the man went through, Poker-facing too much for his liking.
People he had to reintroduce himself to with every circle.
Places Phainon saw again and again — too many times to count.
And the unbearable truth: he had to pretend none of it was happening, again and again, for 33,550,336 loops.

Every time it ended the same.
Every time, he was thrown back in.
And every time, he was angrier than before — a fury born from being reduced to a subject in someone else's twisted experiment. A set of "tests" from people he'd give anything to strangle.
But there was one thing that made it bearable.
One person.
Mydeimos.
The crown prince of Kremnos — at least, that’s who he was in most circles.
While everyone else grated on Phainon’s nerves with every repetition, Mydeimos never did.
Somehow, he slipped past the layers of cynicism and pain and carved out a space in Phainon’s heart.
How did he get so deep?

He still remembers it, the 11,749,992nd circle.
When suddenly Mydeimos acted differently, but he didn't care — he couldn't dare for this chance to slip away.
Phainon had dared to hope.

Maybe this time, they could talk.
Maybe this time, someone would remember him.
But reality had other plans.
Phainon got too attached to Mydeimos.
Phainon saw only him and Mydeimos in the light — yet Mydeimos?
He kept looking past him.
Always out for others. Always playing the prince.
Why?

Why couldn’t he see Phainon — really see him — and the torment he was drowning in?
Mydeimos only wanted the others to open their eyes — to see the truth for what it was: a carefully constructed lie.
While Mydeimos kept saying, "It's to help you,"
Phainon had never needed the help, their help.
He didn’t want pity.

What he longed for was understanding.
For someone to truly grasp the weight he carried —
the endless waiting, the quiet agony,
just for a single chance
to speak with someone who would still remember him
when the circle broke and began again.

Even when the circle continued
Mydeimos remembered him, but never looked his way.
Until the people of Amphoreus decided they simply had a mad crown prince — and looked at him with the same eyes Phainon had been avoiding all this time.
When Cyrene and Lygus noticed it though, the 33,550,336th circle had finished.
It was final, Mydeimos wouldn’t be remembering him now—until god knows when.

Then the next circle began.
And this time… Mydeimos was gone.
“No, no — where is he?!”
Phainon remembered screaming in his head as he tried to look for him.
Everyone else was there.
Everyone except him.

He searched every building, every street, every crack in the pavement.
Nothing.
Just the silence.
Just the words:
“There’s no one by that name.”
Phainon was furious.
At them.
At himself.

He knew Mydeimos wouldn’t be in the same place —
but gone?
Completely gone?
That couldn’t be.
It wasn’t possible.
Not him.

Was this their idea of entertainment?
Tearing someone apart just to see if they'd shatter?
Was it fun for them — to poke, to prod, to wound
until even the quietest screams finally broke through?

Phainon had never cried in a circle before.
Not once.
Not through the pain, the resets, the loneliness.
But now?
Now he wept.
Not out of pain.
But because of the hope, the one thing he had dared to keep.
He was gone just as if he never existed.

Still… he waited.
Surely Mydeimos would come back.
Surely it was just a bug. A glitch. A hiccup in the system.
These two insufferable fuckers would never keep someone out of a system, right?

So Phainon kept going.
Circle after circle after circle.
Until, one day, it hit him.
He’s not coming back.

There was never a chance.
Just the illusion of one — born from the mistake of letting himself care for a conscious Mydeimos.
Someone who, for once, had seen him as more than a programmed puppet.
Someone who treated him like a person.
Not just a lab rat designed to suffer.
Phainon stood there, bitter and broken.
And finally said it out loud:
“God, fuck this.”

So he did what he should’ve done the moment he realized that
Mydeimos was truly gone.

No more pretending.
No more waiting.
Phainon had a thousand weapons.
A thousand faces.
A thousand carefully crafted words.
And endless knowledge —
all of it would be useless now.

All of it was destined to rot in another circle that would never matter again.
When Phainon stepped into his bedchamber in the so-called Eternal Holy City,
Phainon took the only thing that mattered to Cyrene and Lygus, his greatsword.
“If you do this, the circle will only reset.”
“It’s worth a try.”
“Death is forever.”
“No… death is temporary. We’ve seen that ourselves.”
“But love… love is eternal.”

The voices in his mind whispered like ghosts,
and one by one, they extinguished the last light in his eyes.

He drove the greatsword through the base of his skull —
clean, final, quiet.
Phainon didn’t aim for the heart.
That had always belonged to Mydeimos.

Because if the world was going to forget them both…
at least he wanted to choose how he vanished.

Until they meet once again.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

It was dark. Phainon felt as if he were floating—
Floating through emotions, through memories.
Was this what death felt like?

He thought he saw Mydeimos again, in all his forms.
The darkness wrapped around him—not cold, not harsh, but warm.
Nothing like the stories people told, it was nothing like he thought it would be.

It felt like a long, lingering hug from so many people at once,
So many that he couldn’t breathe—
Only smile.
Until he woke up.

It was still warm.
But this time, it was the sun hitting his face.
The sun?

As he opened his eyes fully, a pale beige ceiling came into view.
There was also the matching beige wall with a small window set into it— some binds in front of it that, frankly, didn't help to keep the sun out at all.
On the windowsill sat a bunny succulent, next to it was a seemingly handmade puppet that looked like a white cat with blue button eyes.
Phainon wasn't too sure about that though...

The window was open just a crack, letting in a soft breeze.
A traditional Japanese glass wind chime hung from the window frame, sending out gentle, tinkling notes with every stir of air.
He looked around. The room was bright.
Not large, but comforting in its simplicity.

The bed he lay in was generous in size, wrapped in soft green bedding.
Nearby stood a wooden desk scattered with papers—covered in a language Phainon wished he could read.
A bulletin board hung on the exact other side, cluttered with pins and loose photographs.
Of course, a wardrobe that was looking old but also in good shape.

Then, the door creaked open.
A man stepped in.
The first thing Phainon noticed was his hair—mint green, pulled into a loose bun. The color looked faded, like it had once been something more vibrant.
His eyes were a pale blue, strangely harmonious with the hair that shouldn’t have matched—but did.

Then Phainon noticed the tray in his hands:
Crackers. A small jar of marmalade.
And a glass of diluted fruit juice.
Altogether, it painted one clear conclusion:
Phainon had been unconscious.

"You're awake?" the man said, his voice soft with surprise.
Now that Phainon saw him more clearly, he realized something odd—the man looked remarkably like Anaxagoras, his old teacher.
But somehow… freer. More at ease.
Like someone who had let go of burdens long ago.
That made Phainon smile, just a little.

But whatever the man had said, Phainon couldn’t understand a word of it. He simply shook his head in quiet confusion.
The man chuckled, apparently mistaking the gesture for sarcasm.
"Eat," he said with a grin. "You weren’t out long, but it’s still good to have something."

He placed the tray on a tiny nightstand that Phainon hadn’t even noticed before. A small reading lamp sat on it, along with a pair of glasses—delicate, silver-framed ones.

Phainon sat up slowly, taking the tray into his lap. There was a butter knife wrapped in a napkin. He unwrapped it and opened the jar of marmalade.
Carefully, he spread it over a cracker and took a bite.
Sweet, slightly bitter—orange marmalade. The color reminded him of Mydeimos. That soft, familiar warmth tugged at something deep in his chest.
His mind raced with questions, tangled in theories and memories, but strangely, his heart remained calm.
If even Anaxa was here—
Then surely Mydeimos was too.
This place, this world, this timeline, whatever it was, it was different.
But it might be enough.
First, though, he had to figure out what Anaxa was trying to say.

Phainon had always been a fast learner. It was one of the traits that endeared him to his teachers.
And now, it would have to serve him once more.

As Phainon nibbled on the marmalade-covered cracker, Anaxa stepped back into the room.
He seemed curious now, a little more focused, maybe even concerned. He spoke again, voice calm but insistent, asking questions one after another:
“What’s your name?”
“Do you know where you are?”

Phainon blinked, staring at him blankly. The words came out smoothly, but they made no sense to him. He could hear the tone, the intent—but not the meaning.
He opened his mouth to respond, unsure of how to explain that he didn’t understand. No words in this foreign tongue came to him.
Instead, instinctively, he spoke in Kremnoen, his native language.

Anaxa stiffened slightly, eyes widening in surprise.
He took a step back, visibly startled.
And then understanding dawned on his face.
He chuckled softly, a mix of relief and realization.
“Ah… so that’s it,” he muttered to himself, more to the air than to Phainon. “To you, English just sounds like static, doesn’t it?”
Phainon nodded slowly since the look on Anaxa's face meant that he finally understood, grateful that something had finally gotten through.
For the first time since waking up, he felt like things were starting to make sense.
Just a little.

As Phainon set the tray down on the small nightstand, he slowly stood up.
Anaxa immediately stepped closer, concern flickering across his face, as if afraid Phainon might lose his balance.
But Phainon stood steady.

There was no doubt in his mind anymore—this was Anaxagoras. His teacher. The same calm presence, the same watchful eyes. Somehow, impossibly, he was here too.

A soft smile spread across Phainon’s face as he looked around the room again. His eyes landed on the desk, cluttered with familiar-looking papers. He stepped over and picked one up—it was a marked test, the handwriting unmistakable.
That smile widened.

Then, he noticed the vocabulary book lying nearby. He grabbed it, held it up, and pointed to it while making a few simple gestures—his best attempt to say: Help me learn this.
Anaxa immediately understood.

“Smart. Learning the language with gestures? Alright,” he said with a fond smile.
Of course, Anaxa understood.
Of course, he’d teach him.
He always had.
And so, in that quiet, sunlit room, they sat down together—teacher and student once more—starting with the basics, slowly weaving together a common language.
A new beginning built on something deeply familiar.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Notes

Anaxa opened the vocabulary book and tapped the first word: “the.”
He spoke it clearly once, then again—slower, more deliberate.
Phainon furrowed his brow and echoed the sound. It came out rough, awkward on his tongue.
Anaxa nodded, approving. “Close enough.”
And just like that, the lesson began.

Word after word, Anaxa spoke. Phainon repeated.
They laughed now and then—especially when Phainon pronounced “coffee” more like “caughee,” brow furrowed in fierce concentration over the vocabulary book.

Between words, they shared more than just language.
Anaxa told Phainon to simply call him “Anaxa,” then went on about his job, how he lived, and just little things.
Phainon offered facts in return—his age, his fighting skills, fragments of his knowledge—like that he found out that besides the language, nothing was so different here.
The Math was the same, just as most of the Physics and everything around it.

Time blurred.
With every word linked to an object, every sound to a meaning, Phainon felt the fog in his mind lift. The disorientation loosened its grip. Memory stirred. He felt more here.
At one point, Anaxa paused. He looked at Phainon with an expression that was hard to name—part pride, part something heavier.
“It feels like I’ve been teaching you for ages,” he said softly. “Like you’re an old student of mine. You adjust well.”

Phainon understood every word. And the fact that he could understand all of it made him proud.
But it also scared him. Should he explain how he already partly knew Anaxa?
His reaction must have shown on his face because Anaxa stood up and stretched.
“How about I show you around town?” he asked, smoothing his hair in the mirror.
Phainon realized then—he hadn’t looked in a mirror since he arrived.
(He didn't even notice that Anaxa had one...)
If Anaxa looked different in this world… would he too?

He rose and stepped beside him. His clothes were different—Anaxa must have changed them.
But that raised a bigger question: how had Anaxa found him?
There was no way he had just shown up in Anaxa’s bed and it was all fine, no questions asked.
Still, he pushed the thought aside when something else caught his eye: his hair.
It wasn’t white anymore like it had been in Amphoreus.
It was blonde—the same shade he had in his Demiurge form. Familiar, but out of place. Almost unnatural.
Then again, maybe white hair would’ve looked stranger in this world.
Aside from that… nothing else had changed.
And somehow, that felt even stranger.

While Phainon stood there, studying his reflection, Anaxa rummaged through a drawer and pulled out clothes that might fit Phainon.
Not an easy task—Anaxa’s waist was, according to his students, very narrow.
But he found something eventually and tossed them over.
“Get changed and come out. I’ll set out a toothbrush and some other stuff for you.”
Phainon nodded, quickly slipping into the new clothes and stepping into the rest of the apartment for the first time.
Stunned by how it looked.

Phainon had expected the apartment to be spacious, but like the bedroom, it turned out to be rather small. The color scheme matched as well—a soft, light beige that gave everything a warm, soft tone.

A long hallway stretched out before them, leading directly to the front door. Along the walls, a few plants sat on shelves, basking in the gentle sunlight that streamed in.
Drawn toward the light, Phainon noticed a large, arched doorway made of light wood.
It opened into the living room, which was also modest in size.
As he stepped into the living room, he noticed a bookshelf right next to the door, packed with books.
A cozy couch faced inward, backed by a lush wall of plants that looked impressively healthy.
There was also a wide, arched window that brought in more daylight, right next to the couch, complete with a built-in window seat—perfect for gazing outside.
A few pieces of art adorned the walls, and a television was tucked between the art pieces as well.
In the center of the room was a round, inviting carpet that tied everything together.

Phainon started to feel jealous, what if he and Mydeimos lived here?
Would Mydeimos love the colors or rather have another?

As he stood there, Phainon suddenly heard Anaxa’s voice again.
"Come here!"
The call came from somewhere deeper within the apartment. He quickly made his way back into the hall way and spotted Anaxa standing in the middle of it, going into the bathroom, holding up a toothbrush.

"Here—" Anaxa handed it over, along with a tube of toothpaste. "There's the sink. Brush your teeth, and then meet me in the kitchen. We'll figure out where to go today."
The bathroom was even smaller than the other rooms, but it had everything one might need. There was nothing particularly special about it—just the basics.
After brushing his teeth, Phainon found an unused hairbrush and used it to finally tame the mess on his head.

Then he made his way to the kitchen, where Anaxa was already waiting, leaning casually against the counter, phone in hand.
Phainon wanted to look over the kitchen real quick, like with the other rooms but Anaxa quickly grabbed his attention so he couldn't.

"Okay," Anaxa began, "I know where we're going. You need a job—something simple, where you just have to follow a few instructions. We’ll figure it out once we’re outside."
Phainon simply nodded. In response, Anaxa handed him a pair of shoes, explaining that Phainons old ones were in rough shape.

He slipped them on, and the two of them headed out. The weather was warm, so there was no need for a jacket.
As they stepped outside, Phainon took in his surroundings. It didn’t feel like a huge city, but there were still plenty of apartment buildings and houses packed around them—that was the first thing he noticed.

The other thing he noticed was that there weren't many people out that day, it was good though...Phainon didn't want to get overwhelmed already.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

Riding the bus, they passed into a livelier part of town. The crowd outside shifted—suddenly, they were surrounded by people who looked noticeably younger.

As they stepped outside of the Bus Anaxa suddenly spoke up
“This is the university I work for,” Phainon looked around a bit more and
nodded. It made sense.

“The campus is pretty big—you won’t see the main building from here yet. But look, there's the coffee shop.”
He pointed toward a small place tucked just off the street.

“Let’s grab something to drink.”
Without hesitation, Phainon followed Anaxa and as they stepped inside the smell of freshly ground espresso beans released their earthy, slightly bitter aroma, deep and roasted, with hints of dark chocolate and toasted nuts. There's a whisper of steamed milk in the air, warm and creamy, softening the sharper edges of the coffee. Beneath it all, faint traces of vanilla, baked pastries, and maybe a dusting of cinnamon swirl together, creating a scent that feels like a hug in the form of air.

It's not just the smell of caffeine—it’s the scent of quiet mornings, rain tapping on windows, pages turning in a book, and unspoken conversations.

University students were scattered across the space, sunk into worn, comfortable brown chairs, their conversations humming in the background like a soft current just like the soft music around them.
The clean and welcoming counter sat off to the side. A woman with blonde curls moved gracefully behind the espresso machine, steam rising as she worked.
Phainon stood still for a moment, taking it all in.
It felt like a pause in time once again.

As Phainon lingered by the entrance, perhaps a little too long, Anaxa walked past him, heading straight to the counter.
He greeted the woman behind it with a name that caught Phainon off guard.

“Good morning, Aglaea.”

The pretty woman turned. Her eyes were striking—mostly green, with just a hint of blue swirled in. Her lovely hair added to the charm just more. Unlike how she’d seemed in the Circles, unapproachable, she looked different here: grounded, brighter— just like Anaxa, more alive.

“Good morning, Anaxa,” she replied, placing a freshly made coffee on the counter just as someone stood up to take it. They smiled at her, clearly a regular, and she returned it with easy grace.

It was surprising—just as Phainon was studying her, she was studying him too.
“I’ve never seen him here before.” she said, leaning forward slightly and resting her hands on the counter for comfort.

“Yes, he’s… sort of new...” Anaxa replied, his voice trailing off like he had more to say but couldn’t quite shape it into words.
Right. Phainon had just stumbled into this world, and already it felt like everything was racing ahead without him.

“Anyway! You were looking for a part-timer, weren’t you? Well, here’s one!”
Anaxa clapped a hand on Phainon’s shoulder and gave him a gentle shove forward.
Aglaea looked intrigued. She tilted her head slightly, eyeing him with more focus now.
Phainon blinked, thrown off balance. What?!

“Wait—I thought we were just getting coffee?” he said, turning sharply toward Anaxa, but the man brushed his words off completely.
“I think he’d be a good look for the café,” Aglaea chimed in, thoughtful. “People would like him.”

She nodded once, then placed her hands on her hips and smiled—a warm, satisfied smile, the kind someone wears when a plan falls perfectly into place. Like a proud mother who's just secured the best deal at the market.
Phainon wasn’t sure whether to run or laugh. Maybe do both...

He didn’t feel like he had time for all of this.
Sure, he wanted to settle—this place had a pull to it. The warm air, the happy people, the way the light hit the streets.
It felt safe, almost like it wanted him to stay. And a part of him did.

But then there was Mydeimos. The thought cut through everything like a cold wind. He hadn’t forgotten, not for a second. That search still weighed heavy on his chest. And this—this café, these strangers, this job offer that wasn't really an offer—felt like a detour.
A strange and sudden one.

Still, Anaxa and Aglaea were looking at him like he had just been given a golden opportunity, not thrown into a new layer of chaos.
He shifted his weight, unsure.
“I just… I don’t know if I can commit to anything right now,” he said, carefully. “There’s so much I don't know about this place yet."

Aglaea's smile softened, her expression changing just slightly—as if she understood more than she let on.
Anaxa, meanwhile, raised his eyebrows but said nothing at first.
Then, Aglaea spoke up:
“We’re not asking you to stay forever, Phainon. Just long enough to breathe. You’ll still have time to look.”

Phainon stood still for a moment, eyes drifting across the café—the warm tones, the quiet laughter, the gentle clatter of cups. It wasn’t what he’d expected when he woke up that morning.
He hesitated. Then nodded. Slowly.

He still wasn’t sure. But something inside—deeper than reason, deeper than fear—told him he would find what he was looking for. That Mydeimos was still out there.
And maybe… just maybe… life didn’t have to be a straight line.
Not when you’ve been given a second chance.
Not when you finally know what you’re reaching for.

"Good,” Aglaea said, already turning with a brisk, cheerful tone. “I’ll get your uniform now. We’ve got a bunch of sizes in the back—we’ll find something that fits.”
She paused to glance back at him, that same sparkle in her eyes.

“Tomorrow you’ll start. Come early, before customers show up, I’ll teach you the basics without any distractions. Sound good?”

Phainon didn’t answer right away—still wrapped in the hum of his thoughts—but he moved after her without protest. Something had shifted, gently but surely.
He followed Aglaea into the back room, the bell above the door giving a soft chime behind them, like it was closing one chapter and opening another.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

Some time had passed—not much, maybe a week at most, the only thing that really changed was the fact that he was able to get his own small bed at Anaxa's place.
Aglaea wasn’t there that morning, and it was still early. The café was quiet, touched by soft golden light creeping through the windows. Phainon moved with slow, practiced ease. He finally understood how to make good coffee—people had even started praising him for it.
Well... eventually.

At the start, all he heard was: “Where’s Aglaea? Your coffee is so... unique.”
“At least they tried to be nice,” Phainon mumbled, a little tired from the early hour, but amused nonetheless.

He moved through the morning routine—putting down the chairs, wiping the tables, making everything feel fresh again. Outside, a stream of university students hurried past, books clutched to their chests and sleep still clinging to their eyes.
“Early classes must be tough for some,” he chuckled, watching them.
The thought of Mydeimos came without warning— since he was always late to class, never rushing, as if the world would adjust to Mydeimos's timing instead.
Phainon used to wait at the school gate just so they could be late together.
He figured it was less embarrassing that way.

He slipped behind the counter again, preparing for the rush hour.

Suddenly, the bell chimed—Instead of Phainon instantly turning around he still prepared a bit more since most customers needed a moment—or several—to decide what they wanted.
There was often no need to hurry.
But to his surprise, a throat cleared, politely but firmly.
Phainon blinked, realizing he hadn’t turned around yet.
Right.

He spun around, a little embarrassed.
He was met with colored contacts that shimmered purple, almost pink, and her hair, dyed to match, cascaded down her shoulders like cotton candy caught in sunlight.
It was a girl who was most likely a university student, though she stood out.
Phainon blinked again. That was a bold look for class.
Do people even go to lectures like that?

But who was he to judge, he just listened... as he made coffee and tried to keep his world from spinning too fast.
So he smiled politely, ready to take her order.

She didn’t look too amused.

Phainon had a suspicion why—word must have gotten around campus. Just a few days ago, his coffee had been... well, experimental at best.
She stared up at the menu, lips pursed in silent thought. Phainon gave her a polite smile, then glanced outside to avoid the tension. That’s when he noticed someone right outside of the cafe—a person in a wheelchair, waiting quietly.

Their hair was the same pinkish-purple hue as the girl in front of him. It caught the morning light in the same way. He tilted his head slightly in thought, still looking over to her.
Then the girl outside suddenly turned her gaze sharply back at him.
Phainon flinched. Scary.
He straightened up as if he’d just been caught slacking off during an exam.

The person in the wheelchair approached the door—angled just slightly, the way most wheelchair users do to give themselves space. She stopped in the perfect position: close enough to grab the handle, far enough not to get hit when the door swung open.
Phainon found himself watching the motion—quietly admiring the precision, the naturalness of it.

The bell above the door chimed as it opened.
The girl in front of him spun around immediately.
And the person who just came in spoke up “Castorice, did you forget what I wanted to order?”
Her voice was light, but clearly teasing. They matched—same hair, same contacts, a mirrored sort of energy.
Wait... Castorice? Phainon’s eyebrows lifted just slightly.

“Sorry, Polyxia...” Castorice said, looking at her with a sheepish look. Despite seeming older, she didn’t act like it. Not at all.

Both of them turned to face him now. The tension had eased a little—maybe being together grounded them somehow.
“I’d like a cappuccino with cream on top,” Castorice said first, clear and confident.

Polyxia, still scanning the menu with careful eyes, until she finally made her choice.
“I’ll take an iced matcha latte.”
Phainon nodded, slipping into the rhythm of movement as he began their drinks. The hiss of the steam wand, the measured scoop of matcha—it gave him something to focus on, even as his thoughts raced.

How is she even here? Castorice—quiet and distant in the other world—seemed different now. More animated. More... calmed down rather than scared and putting up a wall.
But maybe that was what happened when you were reunited with someone you lost.

He glanced up at them briefly. Polyxia looked alive in a way that tugged gently at something in him. This world had given them what the other hadn’t: time and life.
Even if—even if—Castorice still had shadiness in her eyes.

He set the drinks on the counter with practiced ease.
They both leaned in, inspecting them.
“I really hope this time it tastes good…” Castorice whispered, barely audible—but he caught it anyway.
Ouch.

But then they took their first sips.
And their eyes lit up.
Phainon had to stop himself from visibly patting his own back like he was the crowned king of baristas.
“This is so good! Thank you!” Polyxia beamed.
Castorice stepped forward, pulling out a bill. “Here—fifteen dollars. Keep the change.”
She handed it over with a small nod, then moved to open the door for her younger sister.

Phainon stood behind the counter, watching them go.
It was surreal—how quickly familiar faces were appearing in this new place. How fast the world seemed to pull everything toward him.
But still…

No sign of Mydeimos.
Phainon exhaled slowly, the breath tinged with something between patience and a quiet ache.

The day went by and rush hour? It really rushed.
Not that Phainon was surprised.

Aglaea had warned him she’d be gone for a little while—something about needing time for her own well-being.
He didn’t press her. She always smiled too wide when she was hiding something.

Thankfully, the café had a work phone. One of those chunky old things with a cracked screen and way too many saved contacts labeled things like “Milk (Emergency)” or “Pastry Girl (DO NOT TRUST MAKE IT YOURSELF!)”.

But it worked. He could reach Aglaea, delivery services, and whoever else kept this place humming. It helped keep the chaos in check.
The hours blurred—orders, faces, names he forgot the moment they left—and then suddenly, the sky turned a soft slate gray. A patter of rain began outside, gentle at first, then steady.

Phainon blinked up at the windows.
Time went by that fast?
It was already closing time.
He moved through the motions in reverse—bringing in the chalkboard sign with today’s special—Hazelnut Mocha, apparently a hit—wiping tables, flipping chairs, brushing away dust that somehow always found a way to return.

He saw so many faces today. Each one a stranger. Each one he studied, maybe a little too closely.
Because deep down, Phainon was starting to get scared.
Scared that one day he might forget the face of the man who had brought him here in the first place.
Mydeimos.

That name stayed close to his chest. Too heavy to carry, too precious to drop.
The café felt hollow now—emptied of noise, of warmth, of purpose.
But still, he smiled faintly to himself as he locked the door.
“Well… it was nice seeing someone sort of new today,” he murmured into the stillness.

He walked home through the soft rain, the umbrella forgotten somewhere as usual. And when he reached Anaxa’s house, he barely managed to kick off his shoes before crashing face-first onto the bed again.
Another day done.
And still, the waiting continued.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

When Phainon woke up, the rain was still coming down—not as heavy as during the night, but steady enough to turn sidewalks into puddle traps.
He sighed and muttered to himself, “Let’s hope I don’t fall into one of those today…”

“Phainon, I made breakfast!”
Anaxa’s voice echoed from the kitchen.
Phainon groaned and let his head fall back onto the pillow. That line—he didn’t want to hear it from Anaxa, his old teacher, no matter how kind.
He wanted to hear it from Mydeimos.
His voice. His tone.
Not this… mentor-turned-roommate who made eggs and gave lectures.

“Phainon, if you don’t come I have to throw it away!!”
That snapped him up. He threw on his work uniform in a blur and shuffled into the kitchen—
Only to stop in surprise.
A beautifully made ichigo sando sat on the table. Soft, fluffy white bread, layered with whipped cream and bright fresh strawberries. It looked too perfect to eat.
But he did anyway.
“Thank you!” he grinned, already mid-bite.

Anaxa chuckled from across the table. “You didn’t even chew.”
Phainon shrugged with his mouth full, as he finished he darted into the bathroom to brush his teeth.
From the kitchen, Anaxa called out, “Aglaea won’t be at work again today.”
Phainon nearly choked on toothpaste foam.
“AGAIN?”

“She said today’s usually light. Since there aren't many courses.”
Phainon spat, rinsed, and wiped his mouth with a towel.

“Well, good to know,” he grumbled, already slipping on his shoes.
“I can’t come with you today—my course is way later,” Anaxa added, walking over and handing Phainon something.
A bus ticket.
Not a one-use slip, but a proper, unlimited transit pass.
Phainon blinked. “Woah?! When did you make this?”
Anaxa only shrugged with a sly smile.
“Sure, keep your wizard secrets to yourself…” Phainon teased. They exchanged a grin.
“Alright, see you!” Phainon called out as he opened the door and stepped outside into the hallway.
But the door flew open again.

“Phainon!”
He turned—just in time for something metallic to bonk him on the head.
“Ow—!”
Keys hit the ground with a dull clink.

“Your own, oh and...here,” Anaxa said from the doorway handing him an umbrella, then disappeared back inside.
Phainon rubbed his head, scooping them up.
“Wow… give them to me like the umbrella, not—literally thrown at my skull,” he muttered.
Still, he smiled.

Pocketing the keys, he started walking.
To the bus stop, this time with an umbrella that kept him dry.

On his usual path to the café, Phainon walked briskly through the wet streets.
The rain had finally softened to a drizzle, but today’s duties included something new.
He rolled up the café’s awning carefully, letting it stretch out above the doorway.

No one likes walking into a cafe that is slippery and wet and
This way, the entrance stayed dry and clean.
From there, it was the routine:
Tables, chairs, specials board.
Wipe down the counter.
Fix his bedhead in the reflection of the espresso machine—barely effective.

“Ugh... this is so normal now. Annoying.”
Routine didn’t sit well with him. It reminded him too much of the other times.
The life he’d lived before.
Still, this normalcy was… quieter. Softer. Not bad.

He turned on the café’s battered old work phone, only to be greeted with a name that made him squint:
"Pastry Girl (DO NOT TRUST MAKE IT YOURSELF!)"

“Seriously, who had this phone before?”
Cruel. And yet oddly specific.
The message itself was short:
"Hello, I will come today at 8am."
He checked the time:
7:58.
Just Perfect.

He nodded to himself and tucked the phone away, already moving to the door to prepare for unloading.
Then—the chime of the cafe bell.
The door swung open and in stepped a girl with a sly, cat-like grin, umbrella twirling casually in her hand.
Bright eyes. Confident posture. She didn’t walk into a room—she arrived.
“Oh, you’re new, right?” she asked, cocking her head. “Man, I thought I’d see Aglaea…”
Phainon blinked.
Why does everyone act like it’s disappointing when it’s me?

Did he radiate “backup plan”?
Before he could respond, she offered her hand.
“I’m Cipher. Come help me get the pastries out of the car, yeah?”
He took her hand, mostly out of reflex, and she shook it like she was testing his grip strength.
Her gaze darted up and down in that familiar way.
Almost like Aglaea had done.
Why does everyone here look at me like I’m a particularly interesting cut of meat?
Is that the special thing of this café?

As they stepped outside, they unloaded everything quickly and headed back in.
Phainon was impressed—not by Cipher’s strength, but by the fact that she’d carried everything in goddamn heels.

“I can handle the rest,” Phainon said. Cipher gave a quick nod and walked straight out the door.
She really did move like a cat... though a somewhat arrogant one.
Back in the old world, Phainon hadn’t known her all that well.
Still, it was nice to see that she and Aglaea apparently remained friends.
As he arranged the pastries in the display case, the doorbell chimed again.

“Did you forget something?” he called without looking up, still focused on the layout.
But when he finally glanced toward the entrance, he was met by the sight of a guy's...
blond hair fading into red, clearly dyed.
It was cut short,
his outfit hung loosely, casual, and comfortable.

Glasses in front of his eyes so he could see better.

No way...
“Uh... no,” the guy said. “Can you take my order, please?”

Chapter End Notes

Hello everyone!
I wanted to make this an extra long chapter… I’m sorry if it feels a little rushed at any point... I’ve been sitting here writing for about 5 hours straight :’)

Still, I had a lot of fun putting this one together, and I really hope you enjoy reading it as much as I enjoyed writing it!
Due to the length I am afraid that I made a lot of mistakes so I am sorry if I did..

A little note:
The part about waiting by the gate was actually inspired by one of my real-life friends. Back in school, whenever I was running late for class, he would wait for me at the front so it wouldn’t feel as embarrassing walking in late alone. That small gesture always stuck with me.

chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

In front of Phainon stood, really, truly...him.

"My-"
He wanted to say his name. He really did. But his mind spun wildly.
What if he got creeped out?

"How do you know my name?"
"Do I know you?"
YES. YES, YOU DO. PLEASE REMEMBER ME.

Phainon’s head was reeling. His heart was pounding faster than in those dreams he used to have about Mydeimos.
This was it. He couldn’t let the moment slip away.
Be cool, Phainon. Be… cool.

“Are you also at the university?” he asked, trying to be casual.
He had to check—maybe he was another student as well.
If not… well, he’d have to get his number immediately (though honestly, that was the plan either way).

Mydeimos looked at him, a little confused—maybe because it was a rather personal question, or perhaps it was just so obvious that no one ever thought to ask him.

“Uh… yeah, I am,” he said, glancing toward the door.
Oh no. Oh god. He’s already trying to escape, isn’t he?
“Ah, I see! Never saw you around, so I was surprised. Sorry,” Phainon replied quickly...maybe too quickly, even for his taste.
“So… will you take my order now?” Mydeimos asked, eyebrow raised.
“Alright. What would you like?” Phainon asked, doing his absolute best to sound normal.
“One Mint Mojito Iced Coffee, please.”

Phainon had to smile at that. Most people choose something fast and easy to say.
Of course, Mydeimos doesn’t.
“To here or to go?” Please say to here. Please, to here, please oh please, he begged to the new gods above.
“To go,” Mydeimos replied nonchalantly.
Okay, wow. So the new god is evil. Noted.

“Alright… name?” Phainon asked, stalling. He had no clue how to keep the conversation going.
He had imagined this scene a thousand times—why was it so hard now?
Mydeimos noticed. He chuckled as Phainon clumsily fumbled with the cup.
“Mydei,” he said, smiling.
It was a soft, reassuring smile.
But it wrecked Phainon.
He nearly dropped the cup.
“okAy,” he stammered, a small voice crack in it too.

It was strange. In the old world, Mydei was a nickname—but Mydeimos had always been so picky about who could use it.
Just like Anaxa, who used to get annoyed when people called him anything but Anaxagoras.
Still, it was… nice.

Phainon began preparing the drink, taking every step carefully.
Not just to make Mydei stay a bit longer— really not!
Okay, maybe a little...
but also because he had to get it perfect.
Mint Mojito Iced Coffee was a bold flavor combo—bright, minty, barely sweet.

But Phainon remembered something.
Something important.
Mydeimos had a sweet tooth.
So, of course, he added a puff pastry tart with ricotta and strawberries.
No charge. No explanation. Just… instinct.
He set the drink and the tart down. Mydeimos raised an eyebrow.

“I didn’t order a tart…” he said, pointing at it.
“I know…” Phainon replied, scrambling for a not-stalker excuse.
“Well, a lot of people pair Mint Mojito Coffee with something sweet. It’s a great combo. Just… a tip from the house.”
Phainon winked, but he got embarrassed quickly.
'God damn, this was unnecessary." Phainon thought to himself right after.
Immediately, his face flushed red.

Mydeimos laughed out loud. Then toned it down to a chuckle.
“Well, thank you. I’ll enjoy it… Phainon,” Mydei said, gathering his order and leaving.
Phainon’s heart skipped. He said his name. His name! Finally hearing it again felt like heaven to Phainon.
He could panic and have hope 'How do you know me?!' and all that, but...
It was on the name tag. But still.
He didn’t need to act like some dazed heroine in a romance novel who had hope that they would still have a little bit of a connection.
But, well...He was the dazed heroine in a romance novel right now.

“I wish he’d remember me too…” Phainon sighed, leaning on the counter, deflated.
A moment passed.
“Wait—DID HE EVEN PAY?!” Phainon yelped, jumping upright.
He’d been so lost in his daydreams, he hadn’t noticed.
And Mydei just walked out. How rude.

"I will get you, Mydei." Phainon smiled, looking like a dazed puppy just waiting for his owner to come back.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

A few days went by.
Just as another day passed quietly. A few students drifted in, some settling into seats, others ordering in a rush—probably late for class.
It was almost comical how many people either arrived too late to their courses… or didn’t show up at all.

Phainon rarely skipped back then. He always felt a bit guilty at the thought.
Even on days when he was sure he wouldn’t learn much, he still went.

The café remained calm—until, suddenly, just when evening arrived, soft rain began to fall.
The sky had turned a soft gray. Phainon stepped out, unfurling the awning and hurrying to gather the cushions from the outdoor benches and chairs. He carried them inside before they could get soaked.
No one wanted them damp and musty—Aglaea had once told him about the time they’d nearly molded. It had almost ruined the café’s reputation.

He stacked the last of them neatly in the back, out of the way, just as people began running past the windows.
Classes must have just ended—students hurrying to get home before the rain grew worse.
Phainon smiled to himself.
He always kept a small umbrella in his bag. Just in case.

The bell above the door jingled—a sharp sound against the soft backdrop of rain and the low hum of conversation.
Phainon looked up.

It was a girl. As she closed her umbrella and stepped inside, it was easy to tell—it was Castorice.

To be honest, Phainon hadn’t expected her to come back. Not that he minded. Just... surprising.
He was about to ask why she was alone when she stepped aside and held the door open.
A second later, someone came barreling in, practically slipping on the threshold.
"YOU LEFT ME ALL ALONE IN THE RAIN?! And you had an umbrella!" the newcomer shouted.

It was Mydei—loud, unmistakable, and completely soaked. Dripping from hair to shoes, like he'd walked through a waterfall rather than a drizzle.
Running in the rain was never a good idea anyway.

Sure, it felt like a good plan, but in reality, it just increased the surface area catching raindrops, and with water hitting from all directions—especially the sides—you just end up wetter than if you'd just walked.
Of course, none of that mattered at this moment.

Everyone in the café turned to look. The quiet atmosphere cracked like a dropped plate.
“…Shit,” Mydei muttered when he noticed the stares. His volume finally dropped.
Castorice giggled, clearly unbothered.

Phainon saw the discomfort flicker across Mydei’s face. Without hesitation, he grabbed a towel from behind the counter—the kind they kept around for spills or emergencies—and made his way over.

“Here,” he said, offering it. “Dry off. You can sit in that corner, it’s quieter over there.”
They both nodded and made their way to the spot Phainon had pointed out—partially hidden, away from curious eyes.
So… they’re back. And together this time? Friends, maybe?
Phainon wasn’t sure.

He returned to the counter, taking a few new orders, wiping down tables, letting the hum of the café settle again.

Mydei rubbed the towel over his head with theatrical frustration, sending a few stray droplets flying. Castorice had already made herself comfortable, arms crossed on the table, chin resting on her wrist, watching him with clear amusement.

“I swear,” Mydei muttered, “you’re the worst.”
“Hey, I saved the umbrella,” she replied with a smirk. “You just didn’t walk fast enough.”

As Phainon arrived at their table, pen and notepad in hand, more out of habit than necessity. He gave them a small smile, eyebrows raised.
“So, what will it be?”

Castorice thought for a moment before replying, “Something warm. Not too sweet. Surprise me.”
"Same but something sweeter." Mydei said right after, Phainon simply nodded.

He returned to the counter and set to work. Something about the two of them together made the place feel... different. Not in a bad way, just louder, more alive. Castorice had always looked lonely, but she seemed so alive now...and Mydei? He was always eye candy. Well, at least for Phainon...

As the milk steamed and spices blended, Phainon found himself glancing back at their corner. Castorice was talking quietly, and Mydei was listening, drying his glasses on a napkin. Their body language was... familiar. Comfortable. It was hard to tell if they were just friends or, perhaps, more.

Phainon cursed. There is no way that could be possible.

The drinks were ready in a few minutes. One was a spiced milk tea with cinnamon and cardamom for Castorice. The other, a mellow hazelnut-cocoa blend for Mydei—warm and soft.
But as before, he put a small cookie to Mydeis order, bringing it over.

As both looked up, they quickly took the order.
“Thanks,” Castorice said. She met his gaze for a moment—neutral, but not cold.
“Appreciate it, man,” Mydei added, already pulling the cup close.

“Ah, sorry to bring it up but… Mydei, you didn’t pay for your drink last time,” Phainon said, a little nervously.
He'd never actually had to remind anyone to—well—pay, before.

Mydei looked up, confused for a second, then his face lit with realization.
“RIGHT! Oh god, sorry!” he said, fumbling for his wallet. He pulled out four dollars and was about to hand it over when Castorice suddenly stopped him.

Phainon blinked, caught off guard, especially when he saw the look she gave him.
She was staring at Mydei—intensely—then flicked her gaze toward Phainon, tilting her head slightly in his direction. It wasn’t rude, but there was definitely something unspoken going on.
Mydei hesitated, chewing the inside of his cheek.

“Ugh, just do it,” Castorice muttered, clearly impatient.
He looked a little embarrassed. Maybe even anxious.
Phainon started to worry.
Wait… was the drink that bad last time? Did he feel like it wasn’t worth paying for? Oh god.

"Fine, but- it's embarrassing when you're here, Castorice, " Mydei whispered to Castorice. It was just for her to hear it, but Phainon also heard it.
Castorice rolled her eyes and stood up.
"Bathroom time or some," she said and quickly went across the cafe.

Phainon looked after Castorice and then back to Mydei, who was also staring at him.
“Was… was the drink not to your liking?” Phainon asked, trying not to sound as anxious as he felt.

Mydei’s head snapped up. “NO! No, no—it was really good!” he said quickly, then looked down at his phone and began tapping the table with his fingernail.
Then, after a pause, he added softly, “Sorry if this is weird, but… could I—just, technically—have your number?”
Phainon blinked.
That was what this was about?

A smile spread across his face. Mydei was this nervous just to ask something like that?
How silly.
“Pfft—sure,” Phainon said, pulling his phone from his back pocket.
Mydei brightened instantly, already grabbing his own phone.
Phainon pulled up his contact QR code, holding it out for Mydei to scan. He did it, a little too fast, as if scared the moment might vanish if he waited too long.

Funny. Phainon had imagined it would be him asking Mydei for his number, not the other way around.
Mydei sent Phainon a quick "Hello!" Message to see if it was working.
Phainon showed that he got the message and turned around.

Then, unexpectedly, Mydei reached out and grabbed his hand.
Phainon yelped quietly, surprised and a bit flustered.
“Here. The payment,” Mydei said, placing the four dollars in Phainon’s hand.
“…Thanks,” Phainon murmured as Mydei let go.

Right on cue, Castorice returned, sliding back into her seat. Phainon turned and wandered off, heading back to the counter to wipe down a few tables.
“FINALLY. I couldn’t stand you talking about him so much,” Castorice whispered to Mydei with a sly grin.

Mydei just stared at Phainon’s back, suddenly regretting choosing the corner table. It was too far, too tucked away.
“You look like a creep,” Castorice said casually, sipping her drink.
“I look like crap?” Mydei blinked at her, apparently mishearing.
“That too.”
She didn’t clarify, just turned her gaze out the window again.

“Do I really?” Mydei groaned, tugging at his damp hoodie. “God, the rain ruined me.”
He nibbled on the cookie that Phainon put to his order, hoping Phainon didn’t mind that he looked like a drowned street rat.
“God, shut up,” Castorice muttered, stealing a few crumbs from the cookie that landed on his plate without asking.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

Outside, the sky had deepened into dusk.
The rain had finally stopped, leaving the streets glistening under the dim café lights. Castorice stood and stretched slightly.

“I’m heading out for the night,” she told Mydei.
He nodded in response. “Get home safe.”

With a short nod back, she made her way to the counter and placed a few coins beside a jar of coins, apparently for tips.
“Bye, Phainon,” she said, giving a small wave to show she'd paid.
Phainon looked up from where he was tidying the space—at this point, only Castorice and Mydei remained.

“Bye-bye!” he replied with a smile, waving as she stepped out the door.
She paused once outside, glancing back at Mydei through the window for a moment before vanishing into the night.

Phainon went around the corner toward the table where they’d been sitting, ready to collect the empty cups—assuming, naturally, that both had left.
But Mydei was still there.
He was just… sitting. Quietly. Staring.

Phainon startled slightly. “Ah! You’re still here,” he blurted out. He didn’t want to sound rude, but it had genuinely caught him off guard.
“Yes,” Mydei said, rising slowly. “I wanted to talk to you.”
He was a little shorter than Phainon—not by much, but noticeable now that they were standing close.
“Oh,” Phainon said, shifting his weight as he picked up the cups anyway. “About what?”
He turned and started walking back toward the counter. Mydei followed a step behind.

“Well, first question—where do you come from? I’ve never seen you around,” Mydei asked. Phainon tensed slightly.
Right. I fell from the heavens; only God knows what universe this even is and why I’m here.

But instead of saying that, he smiled.
“Yeah… just sort of ended up here. Trying to build a new life.”
He stepped into the kitchen, starting to rinse the cups. Mydei didn’t hesitate to follow, ignoring the ‘Employees Only’ sign like it wasn’t even there.

“Really? So you live alone?” Mydei asked, still hanging in the doorway.
“No,” Phainon replied, voice calm. “I live with a professor from the university. He kind of… took me in.”
That answer seemed to catch Mydei off guard. His expression shifted slightly, curious.

“Well, that’s… unusual,” he said, with a small blink.
“How old are you, anyway?”
“Twenty-three. You?”
“Twenty,” Mydei said, shifting from one foot to the other.

There was a pause, just long enough to be noticed, before he added, “Ever thought of dyeing your hair? Blue would look good on you.”
It wasn’t really a question. More of a casual declaration.
Phainon looked over his shoulder, a bit amused. “Not really into it... You do, though. Right?”

“Yeah,” Mydei said, reaching up to gather his hair into a quick ponytail. “Been doing it since I was sixteen.”
Phainon glanced back at him.
“Looks good,” he said—then immediately looked away.
That slipped out. That HELLA slipped out.
Mydei chuckled quietly. “Thanks.”

He didn’t tease, didn’t press. Just kept watching while Phainon returned to rinsing cups and stacking plates.
Most people at this point might’ve said ‘Want to help me clean?’, but Phainon knew better.
Mydei and cleaning? That was just a polite way of saying Prepare to break three plates and possibly set something on fire.
So he said nothing. And kept scrubbing.

“You’re really fast at that,” Mydei said eventually, nodding toward the growing stack of clean cups.
Phainon smiled faintly. “You get good when you do it every day.”
Another pause.
Then—

“Hey… you said you were trying to build a new life,” Mydei said, his voice softer this time, more careful. “Does that mean… something happened? Like, before?”
Phainon hesitated—just for a second—then kept washing.

He didn’t answer right away. Not because he was trying to be mysterious… he just didn’t know what answer would sound normal.
“A lot of things happened,” he said finally. “But nothing worth running from. Just… starting fresh.”

Mydei nodded slowly, as if trying to read between the lines.
“I get that,” he said. “Sometimes it’s not about running. Just... breathing differently, somewhere new.”

That made Phainon look up, briefly surprised by the phrasing. Mydei didn’t seem to notice—he was staring at a bit.

Suddenly Mydeimos asked
“You really don’t mind me being back here?” motioning vaguely toward the kitchen.
Phainon raised an eyebrow. “A little late to ask that now.”
Mydei grinned. “Fair.”

Another beat. Then he shifted, leaning a little more into the doorway.
“You seem... calm. Like, very calm. Even when I’m shouting like an idiot in the middle of a café.”
Phainon chuckled under his breath. “Someone has to balance things out.”
Mydei laughed too, quietly. Then he bit the inside of his cheek again—like earlier.

“You know… You kind of make it hard to leave.”
Phainon blinked. Not out of discomfort, but because he didn’t know how to respond to that. The words hung in the air like steam, faint but warm.
Mydei looked up, eyes wide again, slightly worried he’d gone too far. “Sorry, I mean—uh, I just meant like—it’s nice here. And you’re…”
He trailed off.

Phainon finally dried his hands and turned around, leaning lightly against the counter.
“I know what you meant.”
A small silence passed between them.
“I’m glad you stayed,” Phainon added, almost absentmindedly.
And for the first time that evening, Mydei didn’t say anything. He just smiled.

"I'm finished now, we can go home...thanks for keeping me company.
It's nice to talk to someone while closing up." Phainon spoke and moved closer to Mydei, who, in response, stepped away from the door frame.

“No problem,” Mydei said with a small nod.
Phainon grabbed his bag, and the two of them walked together toward the front door. He flipped the OPEN sign to CLOSED, then stepped outside with Mydei and quickly locked up the café behind them.

The streets were quiet, damp, and glinting under the streetlights.
It was genuinely late.
“So, where are you heading from here?” Phainon asked.
Mydei pointed down the opposite street—one that veered away from Phainon’s route.

“Oh,” Phainon said, trying not to sound too disappointed… though, honestly, he sounded very disappointed.
“I’ve got to get to the train station,” Phainon explained. “We'll see each other another day, then.”
Phainon offered a faint smile and pointed in the direction of the station.

“Yeah. I hope so.”
Mydei nodded, but he looked just as reluctant to part.
"I am always in the Cafe, so come by anytime," Phainon said to make Mydei realise he can just come any day.

“Good night, Mydei,” Phainon said, already turning to head his own way.
But Mydei’s voice called out behind him.

“Phainon!”
He turned.
“Is it okay if I text you…? Just, like—just for fun?”
The way he said it—slightly awkward, clearly shy—was almost painfully endearing.
Phainon smiled, warm and genuine. “Of course you can. Get home safe, Mydei!”
He waved brightly, and Mydei waved back with a grin, walking backward for a few steps before turning toward his way.
Their paths split, but both of them, in their quiet way, were still smiling.

✩₊˚.⋆☾⋆⁺₊✧

Phainon finally arrived home, dropped his bag by his room door, and collapsed into bed with a quiet sigh. His cheeks were warm—blushing, actually.

He felt like a high school girl who’d just gotten a love letter from her crush.
Like bingo—but instead of a prize, he’d won everything.
He pulled out his phone and stared at the screen.
No message from Mydei yet.

Biting his lip, he hesitated… then tapped out a message anyway. Might as well take the first step.

[] I hope you have a pleasant rest of the night and get home safely. :)

He stared at the message for a second longer, thumb hovering…
Then tapped send.
Almost immediately, the “delivered” turned into “seen.”
“Wow. That was fast,” Phainon muttered to himself, heart skipping a little.
A few seconds later, a reply popped up:

[] Yeah, just stepped in the door. Have a good rest of the night, too, Phai.

Phainon blinked. Then giggled.
Phai.
That nickname—it was so casual, so soft, so Mydei—and it made his whole chest feel warm.

Still smiling to himself, phone resting loosely in his hand, he drifted off without even realizing it.
His last thought before sleep took him was simple:
I hope we see each other again tomorrow…
